name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: SMW5 cable fault off Pakistan since 18 Nov
summary: A fault on the SMW5 cable off Pakistan since 18 Nov slows internet; GPS jamming hit Dutch flights on 16 Nov
state: A fault on the SMW5 submarine cable about 11km off Pakistan's coast caused slow speeds and outages from 18 Nov, with HTTP traffic down by as much as 36% per Cloudflare Radar; traffic is being rerouted and the cause is not yet known (The National; Radio Pakistan, citing PTA, 19 Nov). No restoration announcement was found by 24 Nov. Separately, suspected GPS jamming affected dozens of aircraft over the Netherlands on 16 Nov (Aviation24). A cable damage incident and GNSS interference keep Watch.
for_you: Internet users in Pakistan may see slower international connections until the SMW5 fault is repaired. GPS interference is handled by pilots and air traffic control and rarely affects passengers directly.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident (SMW5 off Pakistan) and GNSS interference affecting aviation

sources.title: The National — Pakistan internet problems linked to subsea cable fault
Radio Pakistan — Submarine cable fault may affect internet services in Pakistan: PTA
Aviation24 — Dozens of aircraft affected by suspected GPS jamming over the Netherlands

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
